workshopTitle: Google Antigravity workshop by T M Saravanan

prompts.title: Module 1: The Persona & Role Priming Framework
prompts.content:
Act as an elite Senior Prompt Engineer and AI Solutions Architect. You have 10+ years of experience in system prompt optimization and few-shot reasoning workflows.

Your task is to analyze my business problem and design a modular 3-step prompt chain.

Before providing the final prompt chain, ask me 3 clarifying questions about:
1. Target audience and tone
2. Key constraints or edge cases
3. Desired output format (e.g. JSON, Markdown, Table)
prompts.notes: Encourage participants to test this with GPT-4o or Claude 3.5 Sonnet.
prompts.whyItWorks:
1. Explicit Role Anchoring: Primes the model's weights toward expert terminology and methodical reasoning.
2. Mandatory Clarification Gate: Prevents the AI from guessing assumptions by requiring 3 clarifying questions first.
3. Modular Structure: Breaking the solution into a 3-step prompt chain yields significantly higher quality output than a monolithic prompt.
prompts.howNotToPrompt:
❌ "Can you write me a prompt for my business?"

Why this fails:
• Zero context on your industry, audience, or constraints.
• Leaves the AI guessing tone, depth, and output schema.
• Leads to generic filler that requires 5+ tedious rounds of re-prompting.

prompts.title: Module 2: Few-Shot In-Context Learning Prompt
prompts.notes: Observe how providing few-shot pairs forces deterministic JSON adherence.
prompts.whyItWorks:
1. Pattern Matching (Few-Shot): The LLM sees both negative and positive examples, establishing boundary definitions.
2. Deterministic JSON Schema: Explicit key-value pairs eliminate conversational chatter and enable backend API consumption.
3. Dynamic Input Token: {{USER_INPUT}} cleanly demarcates where real runtime variables get injected.
prompts.howNotToPrompt:
❌ "Classify this customer feedback and tell me if they are mad or want a feature: 'The export button fails!'"

Why this fails:
• Returns conversational paragraphs rather than parseable data.
• Ambiguous category boundaries cause hallucinations.
• Inconsistent labels ('very angry' vs 'mad') break downstream automation.

prompts.title: Module 3: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) Logic Solver
prompts.content:
Solve the following problem step by step.

Rules:
1. Think through the problem inside <thinking> tags step by step.
2. Verify any arithmetic calculations twice.
3. State the final answer explicitly in a box: \boxed{answer}.

Problem:
A company has 120 employees. 45% work remotely, 35% work hybrid, and the remaining work on-site. If 8 hybrid employees transition to fully remote, what is the new percentage of employees working on-site, hybrid, and remote?
prompts.notes: Notice how enclosing thoughts in XML tags dramatically reduces math calculation errors.
prompts.whyItWorks:
1. Scratchpad Reasoning: Enclosing thought processes in <thinking> tags lets the model compute intermediate steps before committing tokens to the final answer.
2. Self-Verification Constraint: Asking to check arithmetic twice activates error-detection attention heads.
3. Structured Extraction: \boxed{...} format makes programmatic evaluation effortless.
prompts.howNotToPrompt:
❌ "What's the answer to this math problem? Don't explain, just give me the numbers."

Why this fails:
• Forcing the model to output the final answer immediately without reasoning steps causes arithmetic errors.
• LLMs calculate token-by-token; denying reasoning tokens drastically degrades math capability.

prompts.title: Create the hero section
prompts.content:
Act as an elite Senior Prompt Engineer and AI Solutions Architect. You have 10+ years of experience in system prompt optimization and few-shot reasoning workflows.

Your task is to analyze my business problem and design a modular 3-step prompt chain.

Before providing the final prompt chain, ask me 3 clarifying questions about:
1. Target audience and tone
2. Key constraints or edge cases
3. Desired output format (e.g. JSON, Markdown, Table)
prompts.whyItWorks:
"Create a single-page React app named 'Campus Idea Wall' using Tailwind CSS.

Requirements:
 1. Top Header: Bold title, subtitle, and an 'Add Idea' button.
 2. Input Form: Fields for Student Name, Department dropdown (AIML, CSE, ECE, Mech), and Idea Textarea with a Submit button.
 3. Idea Grid: Display 4 mock cards in a 2-column layout. Each card shows Author, Dept tag, Idea text, timestamp, and an interactive '▲ Upvote' button.
 4. Design Style: Clean light theme, 2px solid black borders, light grey backgrounds, and soft pastel badges."
prompts.howNotToPrompt:
Prompt B: Fixing Console Errors (Template):
 "I saw this red error in my browser inspect console:
'PostgrestError: new row violates row-level security policy'
 Do not rewrite the entire app. Just tell me the single SQL permission command to paste into Supabase to allow submissions."
